이러한 판례에 대해서는 찬반양론이 있다. lack of cohabitation뿐만 아니라 genotype incompatibility가 되는 경우에도 presumption of paternity가 미치지 않는다고 보아야 한다는 주장도 있고, 판례를 change하여 혼인 중에 출생한 자녀에 대해서는 unlimited하게 presumption of paternity 규정을 apply해야 한다는 주장도 있다. 다수의견은 이 판례를 언급하지 않았고 이 issue에 관해 판단하지 않고 있다.
이 사건의 쟁점은 ① artificial insemination child에 대해서 presumption of paternity 규정을 apply할 수 있는가와 ② 종래 대법원 판례가 인정하고 있던 presumption of paternity exception과는 다른 reason으로 presumption of paternity의 exception을 인정할 수 있는가이다.
genotype incompatibility가 되는 경우에도 presumption of paternity가 미친다는 것은 위에서 본 바와 같다. 종래 대법원 판례에서 outward appearance theory에 따라 인정했던 presumption of paternity의 exception grounds를 still 유지해야 하는지 여부나 판례를 change하여 혼인 중 출생한 자녀에 대해서 unlimited하게 presumption of paternity 규정을 apply해야 하는지 여부는 이 사건의 concrete resolution과 directly related되지 않고, 피고들에 대해서 친생자관계부존재확인을 구하는 원고의 상고이유에도 이러한 주장이 included되어 있지 않다. 다수의견은 위 판례의 change 여부를 다루지 않고 위에서 본 issue에 따라 피고들에게 presumption of paternity가 미친다고 볼 수 있는가에 limited하여 판단한 것이다.
라. action for disavowal of paternity에서 standing을 제한함으로써 생기는 문제를 어떻게 해결할 것인가?
민법은 다음과 같은 amendment process를 거쳐 action for disavowal of paternity의 strictness를 relaxed하였다. 2005. 3. 31. 법률 제7427호로 amended된 민법 제847조 제1항은 action for disavowal of paternity에서 filing period를 ‘남편 또는 아내가 그 사유가 있음을 안 날부터 2년 내’로 정하여 남편 또는 아내가 child에 대한 blood relationship의 truth를 recognize할 때까지 filing period가 진행하지 않도록 하고, true blood relationship에 대한 recognition을 basis로 친자관계 maintenance 여부를 seriously deliberate할 period를 부여하여 presumption of paternity를 deny할 수 있는 practical opportunity를 guarantee하고 있다. 2017. 10. 31. 법률 제14965호 amendment로 newly established된 민법 제854조의2, 제855조의2는 혼인관계가 종료된 날부터 300일 이내에 출생한 자녀에 대하여 원칙적으로 presumption of paternity가 미치도록 하면서도 어머니와 어머니의 전 남편은 action for disavowal permission request를, biological father는 acknowledgement permission request를 할 수 있도록 하여 presumption of paternity를 action for disavowal of paternity보다 simpler method로 exclude할 수 있도록 하였다.
그런데도 여전히 presumption of paternity가 미치지 않는 range를 expand하여야 한다는 주장들이 제기되고 있다. 가장 중요한 reason은 action for disavowal of paternity 규정에서 친자관계의 direct interested parties인 child나 biological father(자녀에게는 biological father에 비하여 action for disavowal right를 allow할 necessity가 더욱 크고 biological father에게 action for disavowal right를 인정할 것인지, 이를 인정할 경우 어떠한 limitation을 할 것인지에 관해서 논란이 많으므로, 이하에서는 child에 limited하여 discussion을 전개한다)에게는 action for disavowal right를 allow하는 규정을 두지 않고 있기 때문이다. 만일 child에게는 any exception 없이 action for disavowal이 allowed되지 않는다면, child의 personality rights를 seriously infringe하거나 법률상 presumed된 father-child relationship과 socially recognized father-child relationship 사이에 marked discrepancy가 생기는데도 이를 correct할 opportunity가 outset부터 blocked되는 result가 될 수 있다.
legislation theory로 민법을 amend하여 child를 비롯한 interested parties에게도 일정한 requirements를 fulfill하는 경우에는 action for disavowal right를 부여하는 것이 desirable하다. 이러한 legislation이 이루어지기 전에 interpretation theory의 차원에서 이 issue를 solve할 수 있는 방안을 찾아볼 필요가 있다. 이 issue를 solve하기 위하여 presumption of paternity 규정이 applied되지 않는 exception recognition range를 더욱 expand하자는 opinion이 제시되고 있으나, 이것은 민법이 presumption of paternity 규정과 action for disavowal of paternity 규정을 마련함으로써 form하고자 한 parent-child relationship의 모습을 해칠 우려가 있고 legal theory로도 accept하기 어렵다. 여기에서는 action for disavowal of paternity 규정에서 standing을 인정하는 남편 또는 아내에 대해서는 그 규정에 따라 친생자관계를 확정하고, action for disavowal of paternity 규정에서 standing을 인정하지 않고 있는 자녀 등에 대해서는 current 민법의 systematic·rational interpretation을 통하여 친생자관계부존재확인의 소로써 친생자관계를 확정하는 방안을 제시해 보고자 한다.
concrete cases를 adjudicate하면서 statutes를 interpret·apply하는 것은 court에 given된 inherent authority이자 mission이고, law text의 connotation과 extension을 both 고려하여 그 range 내에서 possible한 reasonable interpretation method라면 court는 마땅히 constitutional-conforming interpretation에 따라 이러한 method를 adopt해야 한다.
친생부인의 소를 제기할 수 있는 standing을 남편 또는 아내에게 인정하고 있는 current 민법에서는 남편 또는 아내는 친생자 아님을 알게 된 경우 그 날부터 2년 내에 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기하여 자녀와 사이의 legal parent-child relationship을 remove할 수 있다. 그러나 자녀는 친생부인이 되지 않는 한 자신이 natural child가 아님을 알게 되더라도 action for disavowal of paternity로써 presumption of paternity 규정에 따른 legal parent-child relationship에서 escape할 수 없다. 한편 민법은 action for disavowal of paternity 이외에 substantive legal parent-child relationship과 family relation register상의 legal parent-child relationship이 match하지 않을 때 이러한 discrepancy를 correct하기 위한 method로 action for confirmation of existence or nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship 규정(제865조)을 두고 있다. 민법 제865조에 따르면 친생자관계에 interest가 있는 자는 ‘other reasons’를 reason으로 하여 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 제기할 수 있다.
남편 또는 아내는 친생부인의 사유가 있는 경우 action for disavowal of paternity 규정에 따라 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기할 수 있으므로, 이와 같은 reasons를 reason으로 하여 친생자관계부존재확인을 구하는 것은 민법 제865조의 규정에 반하여 allowed되지 않는다. 그런데 child는 presumption of paternity 규정에 따른 presumption of paternity의 effect를 받는 direct interested party인데도 action for disavowal of paternity에 관한 standing이 인정되지 않는다. 그러나 이러한 point만으로 곧바로 direct interested party인 child에 대해서 legal presumed parent-child relationship을 blood truth에 부합시킬 opportunity를 completely exclude하는 direction으로 민법을 interpret한다면, child의 personality rights와 self-determination right, right to pursue happiness 그리고 individual dignity와 gender equality에 기초한 marriage and family relations에 관한 basic rights를 seriously restrict하는 result가 된다. 이는 law가 constitutional norms와 harmonize되도록 interpret하는 것을 statutory interpretation의 principle로 삼고 있는 대법원이 취할 right interpretation method가 아니다. 따라서 민법이 인정하고 있는 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 통하여 위와 같은 unreasonable result를 remove할 수 있는지에 관하여 examine할 필요가 있다. law text의 ordinary meaning에 따르더라도 presumption of paternity 규정의 application을 받는 child에게 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 제기할 수 있다고 interpret하는 것이 possible하고 이와 같은 result가 presumption of paternity 규정과 action for disavowal of paternity 규정을 둔 legislative purpose에 반하는 것도 아니라면, 그와 같은 interpretation을 통하여 child에게 presumption of paternity가 applied되는 result에서 escape할 opportunity를 부여하는 것이 child에게 guaranteed된 constitutional basic rights를 realize하는 reasonable method가 될 수 있다.
먼저 child의 case에는 action for disavowal의 reasons가 있다고 하더라도 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기할 수 없으므로, 이와 같은 reasons를 reason으로 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 구하는 것이 민법 제865조의 문언에 비추어 당연히 prohibited되는 것은 아니다. 그렇다고 하여 presumption of paternity가 되는 child의 parent-child relationship에 interest가 있으면 누구든지 child의 status relation과 관련하여 민법 제865조에 따라 친생자관계부존재확인을 구할 수 있다고 볼 것은 아니다. 위에서 본 것처럼 민법이 action for disavowal of paternity를 제한하는 legislative purpose는 status relation의 early stability, child welfare, marriage family에 대한 third party intervention prevention 등에서 찾을 수 있고 이를 통하여 presumption of paternity가 미치는 child와 couple의 privacy와 marriage family peace를 protect한다. 이와 같은 presumption of paternity 규정의 legislative purpose와 action for disavowal of paternity 규정에서 action for disavowal을 구하는 procedure나 period를 strict하게 규정하고자 하는 purpose를 고려하면 혼인 중에 출생하여 presumption of paternity가 되는 child의 status relation을 dispute할 수 있는 interested parties란 이와 같은 legislative purpose를 훼손하지 않는 range에서 only limited하게 인정되어야 한다. 따라서 presumption of paternity effect를 받는 child는 direct interest를 갖기 때문에 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 제기할 수 있다고 보아야 할 것이지만 그 밖에는 status상·property상 interest가 있는 person이라고 하더라도 special circumstances가 없는 한 친생자관계부존재를 구할 수 없다고 보아야 한다.
child가 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 제기할 수 있다고 하더라도 아무런 limitation 없이 allowed된다고 볼 수는 없다. action for disavowal of paternity 규정은 남편 또는 아내가 cause for disavowal of paternity가 있음을 안 날부터 2년 내에 action for disavowal of paternity를 제기해야 하는 것으로 filing period를 정하고 있다. presumption of paternity가 되는 child가 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 제기하는 경우에도 special circumstances가 없는 한 action for disavowal of paternity 규정을 analogically apply하여 그 filing period를 limit하여야 하는데 그 starting point는 cause for disavowal of paternity가 있음을 알았을 때(자녀가 minor인 동안 그 사유를 알았다면 성년에 이른 날)로 보아야 할 것이다.
이와 같이 presumption of paternity가 되는 child가 친생자관계부존재를 확인하는 judgment를 선고받고 judgment가 final되면 그 judgment의 res judicata effect는 가사소송법 제21조에 따라 third party에게도 effect가 있어 누구도 litigation상으로나 litigation outside에서 그와 같은 action for disavowal의 effect와 contrary되는 주장할 수 없게 되어 presumption of paternity의 effect는 사라진다. 그러나 action for disavowal의 effect를 갖는 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship을 제기할 수 있는 child라고 하더라도 그러한 judgment가 없는 state에서는 곧바로 presumption of paternity의 exception을 주장하거나 presumption of paternity의 effect를 deny할 수는 없다. 즉 위와 같은 action for confirmation of nonexistence of natural parent-child relationship claim을 granted하는 final judgment가 없는 state에서는 presumption of paternity의 effect를 받는 child가 biological father를 상대로 acknowledgement claim을 할 수 없고 biological father도 그러한 child를 상대로 acknowledgement를 할 수도 없다고 보아야 한다.
이처럼 presumption of paternity 규정이나 action for disavowal of paternity 규정의 legislative purpose가 destroy되지 않는 range에서 presumption of paternity 규정에 따른 presumption of paternity의 effect를 rebut할 수 있도록 함으로써 action for disavowal of paternity에서 standing을 strict하게 제한하여 생기는 problems를 solve하는 것이 desirable하다.
이상과 같이 majority opinion에 대한 supplemental opinion을 개진한다."}

{"[2018DA1049]": "We consider 상고이유를 판단한다.

1. Civil Act 제860조는 그 본문에서 “인지는 그 자의 출생 시에 소급하여 효력이 생긴다.”고 하면서 단서에서 “그러나 제삼자의 취득한 권리를 해하지 못한다.”라고 하여 인지의 소급효를 제한하고 있고, Civil Act 제1014조는 “상속개시 후의 인지 또는 재판의 확정에 의하여 공동상속인이 된 자가 상속재산의 분할을 청구할 경우에 다른 공동상속인이 이미 분할 기타 처분을 한 때에는 그 상속분에 상당한 가액의 지급을 청구할 권리가 있다.”라고 규정하고 있다.
However, 혼인 외의 출생자와 생모 사이에는 생모의 인지나 출생신고를 기다리지 아니하고 자의 출생으로 당연히 법률상 친자관계가 생기고(대법원 1967. 10. 4. 선고 67다1791 판결 참조), 가족관계등록부의 기재나 법원의 친생자관계존재확인판결이 있어야만 이를 인정할 수 있는 것이 아니다(대법원 1992. 7. 10. 선고 92누3199 판결 참조). Therefore, 인지를 요하지 아니하는 모자관계에는 Civil Act 제860조 단서가 적용 또는 유추적용되지 아니하며, 상속개시 후의 인지 또는 재판의 확정에 의하여 공동상속인이 된 자의 가액지급청구권을 규정한 Civil Act 제1014조를 근거로 자가 모의 다른 공동상속인이 한 상속재산에 대한 분할 또는 처분의 효력을 부인하지 못한다고 볼 수도 없다. The same applies even if 다른 공동상속인이 이미 상속재산을 분할 또는 처분한 이후에 그 모자관계가 친생자관계존재확인판결의 확정 등으로 비로소 명백히 밝혀졌다 하더라도.
2. 가. According to 원심판결 이유, 원심은 다음과 같이 판단하였다. 인지 이전에 공동상속인들에 의해 분할되거나 처분된 상속재산은 Civil Act 제860조 단서가 규정한 인지의 소급효 제한에 따라 이를 분할받은 공동상속인이나 양수한 자에게 확정적으로 귀속되는 것이고, 이러한 법리는 상속개시 후에 친자관계존재확인의 소의 확정에 의하여 상속인으로 판명된 자가 발생한 경우에도 적용된다. The judgment that a biological parent-child relationship exists between 원고(선정당사자) 및 선정자들(이하 ‘원고 등’이라고 한다)과 소외 1 became final after 피고 1이 피고 2에게 원심 판시 별지 1목록 기재 부동산(이하 ‘이 사건 부동산’이라고 한다)을 처분하고 소유권이전등기를 마쳐준 이후이다. Ultimately, 원고 등은 Civil Act 제1014조의 ‘상속개시 후의 재판의 확정에 의하여 공동상속인이 된 자’에 해당하므로, 피고 1을 상대로 매매대금 상당의 가액지급청구권만을 행사할 수 있을 뿐, 피고 2에게 소유권이 확정적으로 귀속된 이 사건 부동산에 대한 처분의 효력을 부인하지는 못한다.
나. However, 위와 같은 원심의 판단은 다음과 같은 점에서 그대로 수긍하기 어렵다.
1) According to 원심판결 이유와 기록, 다음과 같은 사실을 알 수 있다.
가) 소외 1은 소외 2와 혼인하여 피고 1을 출산한 후 이혼하는 한편, 소외 3과 사실혼 관계를 유지하면서 원고 등을 출산하였다.
나) 소외 1은 이 사건 부동산을 소유하다가 2015. 1. 27. 사망하였다. 피고 1은 2015. 6. 8. 이 사건 부동산에 관하여 상속을 원인으로 한 소유권이전등기를 마친 후, 2015. 6. 25. 피고 2에게 이 사건 부동산을 매도하고 그 무렵 소유권이전등기를 마쳐주었다.
다) 원고 등은 2016. 2. 12. 소외 1과 원고 등 사이에 친생자관계가 존재한다는 확인을 구하는 소를 제기하였고, 2016. 7. 1. 그 인용판결이 확정되었다.
2) In light of the foregoing legal principle, 위 사실관계는 원고 등과 생모인 소외 1 사이에는 원고 등의 출생으로 당연히 법률상 친자관계가 생기고 법원의 친생자관계존재확인판결이 있어야 이를 인정할 수 있는 것이 아님을 보여준다.
Therefore, 원고 등과 소외 1 사이에는 Civil Act 제860조 단서가 적용 또는 유추적용되지 아니하고, Civil Act 제1014조를 근거로 원고 등이 피고 1의 이 사건 부동산에 대한 처분의 효력을 부인하지 못한다고 볼 수도 없다. The same applies even if 피고 1이 이미 이 사건 부동산을 처분한 이후에 원고 등과 소외 1 사이에 친생자관계존재확인판결이 확정되어 그 모자관계가 비로소 명백히 밝혀졌더라도.
다. Nevertheless, 원심이 앞에서 본 바와 같은 이유로 이 사건 부동산에 관한 피고들 명의의 지분소유권이전등기의 말소를 구하는 원고 등의 청구를 배척한 것은, 모자관계의 성립과 Civil Act 제860조 단서 및 제1014조의 적용 범위에 관한 법리를 오해하여 판결에 영향을 미친 잘못을 범한 것이다. 이를 지적하는 상고이유 주장은 이유 있다.
3. Therefore, 나머지 상고이유에 대한 판단을 생략한 채 원심판결 중 원고 등 패소 부분을 파기하고, 이 부분 사건을 다시 심리·판단하게 하기 위하여 원심법원에 환송하기로 하여, 관여 대법관의 일치된 의견으로 주문과 같이 판결한다.

[[별 지] 선정자 명단: 생략]"}

{"[2020SEU616]": "재항고이유를 판단한다.\\n1. Overview of the Case and Issue\\n가. 사안의 개요\\n남성으로 출생한 신청인 겸 사건본인(이하 ‘신청인’이라 한다)은 어린 시절부터 female sex로의 귀속감을 가지고, 사춘기가 되어 얼굴 형태와 체격, voice가 남성적으로 변해가는 것에 정신적 고통을 느꼈으나 자신의 gender identity를 숨긴 채 생활하다 혼인하였고, 성정체성 문제로 혼인한 지 약 5년 10개월 만에 이혼하였다. 이후 신청인은 2018. 11.경 Thailand에 있는 성형외과에서 고환과 음경을 제거하고 여성의 external genitalia 모양을 갖추는 등의 surgery를 받아 여성의 옷차림, hair style을 하고 social life as a woman로서 생활하여 왔다. 신청인은 minor children 2명(twins, born in 2012)을 두고 있는 상태에서 family relations register상 gender entry correction permission application(이하 ‘the permission application in this case’라 한다)을 하였다.\\n원심은, 신청인에게 minor children가 있어 gender entry correction을 허가하는 것이 미성년 자녀의 welfare에 negative effect가 있다는 이유로 이 사건 허가 신청을 기각한 제1심결정을 유지하였다.\\n나. Issue in This Case\\n대법원 2011. 9. 2. 자 2009SEU117 En Banc Decision은 성전환자의 gender entry correction을 허가함에 있어 현재 혼인 중에 있거나 transsexual person에게 minor children가 있는 경우에는 gender correction이 허용되지 않는다고 판단하였다. 이 사건의 issue는 그중 후자에 한하는 것으로, 즉 현재 혼인 중에 있지 아니한 transsexual person에게 minor children가 있는 경우를 gender entry correction의 independent negative requirement로 보는 것이 타당한지 여부이다.\\n2. Determination of the Sex of a Transsexual Person and Correction of the Gender Entry in the Family Relations Register\\n가. 사람의 sex를 결정하는 factors에는 sex chromosomes와 이에 따른 genitalia 등 biological factors뿐 아니라 개인이 스스로 인식하는 male 또는 female으로의 귀속감 및 개인이 male 또는 female로서 적합하다고 socially approved된 행동·태도·성격적 특징 등의 sex role을 수행하는 측면, 즉 mental·social factors들도 포함되는 것으로 인정되고 있다.\\nTranssexualism을 가진 사람의 경우, birth after growth process에서 일관되게 출생 당시의 biological sex에 대한 incongruity와 discomfort·aversion을 갖고 그와 다른 sex에 귀속감을 느끼는 한편 자신이 귀속감을 느끼는 sex에 맞는 role을 지속적이고 firm하게 수행하여 출생 당시와 다른 sex로서 mental·social adaptation이 이루어졌고, further, 일반적인 medical standard에 의하여 출생 당시의 sex라고 평가하기 어려울 뿐만 아니라 genitalia 또는 clothing, hair style 등과 같은 bodily appearance와 sexual relations·friendship 관계 등 personal domains 및 occupation 등 social domains에서 transitioned sex로 recognized, accepted되는 정도에 이르러 social-normative하게도 transitioned sex를 갖추고 있다고 인정될 수 있다면, such a transsexual person may legally be evaluated as having the transitioned sex, not the sex at birth.\\n나. 대법원은 2006. 6. 22. 자 2004SEU42 En Banc Decision에서 위와 같은 취지의 법리로, 성전환자의 성별정정 허가 신청에 관하여 성전환자의 경우에는 출생 당시의 성과 현재 법률적으로 평가되는 성이 달라 sex entry of the family register[which can now be regarded as corresponding to the Family Relations Register under the current Act on the Registration of Family Relations, etc. (이하 ‘Family Relations Registration Act’라 한다)] would fail to publicly disclose the current true status relationship, so the sex legally evaluated at present must be reflected in the family register, and accordingly permitted correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person. Further, because such permission is a decision intended to confirm the current true sex newly legally evaluated according to transsexuality, it was held that the effect of the decision granting permission for correction of the family register or the correction of the gender entry based thereon does not affect the existing status relationship and rights and obligations.\\n그런데 대법원 2011. 9. 2. 자 2009SEU117 En Banc Decision은 성전환자에게 minor children가 있는 경우에는 minor children의 welfare를 우선적으로 고려하지 않으면 아니 된다고 하면서, family relations register의 gender correction으로 인하여 minor children에게 mental confusion과 shock를 줄 수 있고 family relations certificate의 disclosure로 minor children가 social discrimination and prejudice에 exposed되거나 daily life difficulties가 생긴다는 등의 이유로, minor children를 둔 transsexual person의 gender entry correction은 허용되지 않는다고 판단하였다.\\n3. Whether Permission for Correction of the Gender Entry of a Transsexual Person with Minor Children Should Be Granted and the Standard for Such Determination\\nHuman being은 누구나 자신의 gender identity에 따른 personality를 form하고 life를 영위할 right가 있다. Transsexual person도 자신의 gender identity를 바탕으로 personality와 individuality를 realize하고 우리 사회의 equal member로서 others와 함께 happiness를 pursue하며 살아갈 수 있어야 한다. 이러한 rights를 fully exercise하기 위해서 transsexual person은 자신의 gender identity에 따른 sex를 true sex로 legally confirm받을 right를 가진다. 이는 human dignity and value에서 derived하는 fundamental right로서 right to pursue happiness의 essence를 이루므로 maximum으로 guaranteed되어야 한다.\\n한편 minor children를 둔 transsexual person도 parent로서 children를 protect하고 educate하며(Civil Act Article 913), parental authority를 exercise할 때에도 children의 welfare를 first해야 할 duty가 있으므로(Civil Act Article 912), minor children가 있는 transsexual person의 gender entry correction permission 여부를 판단할 때에는 transsexual person의 fundamental rights의 protection과 minor children의 protection and welfare와의 harmony를 이룰 수 있도록 legal interests의 balance를 위한 various circumstances를 comprehensively 고려하여 substantively 판단하여야 한다. 따라서 위와 같은 circumstances를 고려하여 substantively 판단하지 아니한 채 단지 transsexual person에게 minor children가 있다는 circumstance만을 reason으로 gender correction을 불허하여서는 아니 된다. The reasons are as follows.\\n가. 미성년 자녀가 있는 성전환자의 성별정정 허가 여부에 관하여\\n1) Protection of Fundamental Rights such as Human Dignity and Value, and the Right to Pursue Happiness of a Transsexual Person\\n가) All citizens have dignity and value as human beings, have the right to pursue happiness, and shall be equal before the law(Constitution Article 10 preamble; Article 11(1)). Human dignity and value imply that each individual should be respected for his or her unique personality and individuality, and should be able freely to choose and develop the content and direction of life deemed most suitable, thereby forming the self and destiny. A transsexual person, too, as an equal member of our society, has dignity and value as a human being, the right to pursue happiness, and the right to live a life worthy of a human being, and these rights must be protected. Therefore, even when determining whether to grant permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person, such fundamental rights of the transsexual person as a human being must be guaranteed to the fullest extent.\\n나) Considering the role that the distinction and recognition of sex plays in society, it is ultimately consistent with maintaining order in society as a whole and with the public welfare to ensure that an individual’s actual sex and the sex publicly disclosed do not conflict by having the individual publicly confirm and disclose his or her sex in a manner consistent with the sex currently legally evaluated. That a transsexual person publicly obtains legal sex in accordance with his or her gender identity through correction of the gender entry does not in itself have any potential to directly harm other members of society. Rather, if the true sex confirmed according to an individual’s gender identity exists, but the sex publicly disclosed through the Family Relations Register does not correspond to it, and that situation is left uncorrected, there is a high likelihood that confusion and misunderstanding will arise among other members of society as a result.\\n다) It is correct to view the confirmation of sex in both private and public spheres as an essential condition of life for maintaining human dignity, which is determined prior to a person’s position or role within the family order. If permission for correction of the gender entry were denied merely because a transsexual person has minor children, then, contrary to the appearance and actual life formed in accordance with his or her gender identity, the person would be displayed in the official records as the sex before transition, and would be compelled to live an absurd life in which the sex as actually existing and the sex as shown in official records are inconsistent. If such an absurd situation is forced upon the person for a long period until the minor children reach adulthood, the magnitude of the suffering that the transsexual person must endure personally and socially, and the urgency of confronting absurdity in order to exist, would inevitably become immense. Such a result infringes the essential content of the constitutional demand to respect human dignity and value and to guarantee the right not to be discriminated against on the basis of gender identity, and is thus unacceptable.\\n라) An individual’s family life forms the beginning and core of social relationships, and the State must guarantee it(Constitution Article 36(1)). A transsexual person, too, as a member who forms a family within the overall legal order, should be granted equal rights and duties, and the State must protect such rights of the transsexual person.\\nAlthough granting permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with minor children may bring about changes in family relations, this is nothing more than a natural process in which the manner in which the rights and duties of the parent are realized changes accordingly as the fact of one parent’s transsexuality occurs. The parent-child relationship and family order thus formed must also be equally respected and protected within the overall legal order. This does not change merely because the transsexual person is divorced and not presently married, or because correction of the gender entry in the Family Relations Register has been made. A transsexual person with minor children must still exercise the rights and perform the duties that accompany his or her role as father or mother, and is able to do so.\\n2) Welfare of Minor Children\\n가) It is not correct to uniformly conclude that granting permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with minor children by itself causes a major change in the status relationship between the person exercising parental authority and the minor children, or is manifestly contrary to the welfare of the children, or leaves minor children exposed without protection to social prejudice and discrimination.\\n나) Correction of the gender entry merely accepts the actual situation of a transsexual person who has completed transition and reflects it in the official record; it does not newly cause major changes in the status relationship between the transsexual parent and the minor children, or affect the substance of rights and obligations. This is because the personal, social, and legal parent-child relationship between a transsexual person and his or her minor children does not change regardless of whether it is before or after correction of the gender entry. Nor can the correction of the gender entry itself be regarded as impairing the essential and core content of the transsexual person’s status and role as father or mother within the family system, or the rights of the minor children.\\n다) Even if minor children in some cases suffer mental confusion and shock due to a parent’s transsexuality, such confusion and shock arise because the parent has already undergone the transition, making it an irreversible fait accompli. Correction of the gender entry is a measure that corrects the sex entry in the official record so that a person who has already transitioned in social common sense can be legally evaluated as having the transitioned sex. Therefore, one must not hastily conclude that the permission itself for correction of the gender entry, which can be said to be the final stage of the transition process, causes mental or psychological shock to the minor children.\\nLikewise, the premise that adult children can accept a parent’s correction of the gender entry without much confusion, whereas minor children will suffer mental confusion and shock, is also incorrect. This overlooks the possibility that minor children, with their flexible minds, may naturally accept the existence of a transsexual parent.\\n라) If an emotional and familial bond has already formed between the transsexual person and the minor children based on the transitioned sex of the father or mother, then it is desirable to grant permission for correction of the gender entry even for the sake of the minor children.\\nFurthermore, even in cases where the minor children have not yet adapted psychologically to the transitioned sex of the father or mother and are suffering psychological and emotional difficulties, if a divorced transsexual father or mother, through correction of the gender entry, provides a social and economic foundation enabling him or her to continue stably raising and supporting the minor children as a parent and an opportunity to seek understanding of transsexuality, this can ultimately serve the welfare of the minor children in that it may restore the bond between them. This is because a transsexual person whose actual sex conflicts with the sex publicly disclosed in the Family Relations Register may in some cases find it difficult in society to choose a job suited to appearance or to engage in economic and social activities corresponding to ability and aptitude, and the minor children of such a transsexual person are likely, while observing such father or mother, to become emotionally more unstable and to face the risk of being placed in a financially poorer environment.\\nTherefore, without examining the various situations existing or arising between the transitioned father or mother and the minor children, the court may, in a substantive sense, fail to act in accordance with the welfare of the minor children by barring correction of the gender entry merely on the ground that there are minor children.\\n마) It cannot be concluded that, if permission for correction of the gender entry is granted to a transsexual person with minor children, the minor children will be left exposed without protection to social discrimination and prejudice or placed in difficulties in daily life merely because of the submission or disclosure of the corrected Family Relations Register.\\nEven if there is a concern that disclosure of the Family Relations Register may expose the minor children to social prejudice and discrimination, the State should protect the minor children by taking measures to block such disclosure for the purpose of safeguarding the fundamental rights and privacy of transsexual persons and their minor children; it is not proper to use that concern as a reason for refusing permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with minor children.\\n(1) Our society has for quite some time now recognized transsexual persons, regardless of whether correction of the gender entry is granted, by assessing a person’s sex normatively according to individual and social recognition, and not merely the biological sex at birth. In reality, transsexual persons are a minority in our society, but as neighbors they live ordinary daily lives like everyone else, and many of them increasingly communicate actively by revealing the forms of their lives through the mass media and the like. Although the level of average understanding of transsexual persons in our society has increased, it is also true that discrimination against and exclusion of transsexual persons still exist in our society. As a result, if the fact that the sex of a transsexual father or mother has been corrected is disclosed to the outside through the Family Relations Register, de facto discrimination may arise for the minor children. However, such a problem can be solved by the State’s improving the contents and procedures of the Family Relations Register system and taking measures to prevent the fact of a transsexual person’s correction of the gender entry from being disclosed, thereby protecting the privacy of transsexual persons and their minor children.\\nAlso, in light of the spirit of our Constitution, which places human dignity as its ultimate goal, the State bears the duty to be careful that acts unlawfully exposing matters related to correction of the gender entry in an individual’s Family Relations Register to the outside do not occur, and to make legal and institutional efforts to correct prejudice and misunderstanding on the part of those who discriminate against transsexual persons or their families; yet refusing permission for correction of the gender entry in the Family Relations Register of a transsexual person on the above grounds is difficult to accept, because it abandons the State’s fundamental duty to prevent harm that transsexual persons and their minor children may suffer from social prejudice and to guarantee the stability of family life.\\n(2) The Personal Information Protection Act was enacted on March 29, 2011 and came into force on September 30, 2011 in order to promote the rights and interests of citizens and realize individual dignity and value, and the Family Relations Registration Act has also improved the problem that personal information was easily disclosed for the protection of individual privacy.\\nThe current Family Relations Registration Act, in principle, allows certificates containing only essential information for each type of certificate to be used, allows the applicant to obtain a certificate by selecting only the information necessary for the purpose of use, or restricts the persons entitled to request issuance of a certificate, and newly introduced certificates in the form of partial certificates showing only some recorded items. Meanwhile, a person requesting submission of a certificate must request a certificate containing only the minimum family relation registration information necessary for the purpose of use, and use of a submitted certificate for purposes other than the purpose of use is prohibited.\\nUnder the Family Relations Registration Act, only the person concerned, his or her spouse, parents, or children may inspect the Family Relations Register(Article 14(7)); only the person concerned, his or her spouse, or lineal blood relatives may obtain certificates under the Family Relations Registration Act(Article 14(1)); and in the case of obtaining a family relation certificate for a minor child, either the father or the mother may be selected, and a family relation certificate(specific certificate) certifying the parent-child relationship only between that parent and the child may be issued(Articles 15(4) and (5), Article 21-2 of the Rules on the Registration of Family Relations, etc.).\\nAlso, due to the enforcement of the Electronic Government Act, schools, administrative agencies, and public institutions, unless special circumstances exist, process matters that can prove family relations after verifying them in an information system available within the scope of the relevant duties without requiring submission or presentation by the party.\\n(3) In light of the current statutory provisions and the social reality concerning the operation of the system as described above, the possibility that, at the stages of inspection, issuance, and submission of a family relation certificate for a minor child, the fact that the minor child’s father or mother has had the gender entry corrected will be carelessly disclosed to a third party is low.\\n3) Current Status of International Norms and Global Trends Regarding Correction of the Gender Entry of a Transsexual Person\\nArticle 2 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights provides: “Everyone is entitled to all the rights and freedoms set forth in this Declaration, without distinction of any kind, such as race, colour, sex, language, religion, political or other opinion, national or social origin, property, birth or other status.” On July 15, 2016, the United Nations Human Rights Council reaffirmed that all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights and are entitled to the freedoms and rights set forth in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, and adopted a resolution opposing violence and discrimination worldwide based on sexual orientation and gender identity, and our country, as a member state, voted in favor of that resolution.\\nAlso, the majority of countries in the world, including Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the Netherlands, Sweden, and the United States, permit correction of the gender entry for transsexual persons, and most countries except Japan do not treat the fact that a transsexual person has minor children as an absolute reason for denying correction of the gender entry. Therefore, refusing to permit correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person merely because the person has minor children runs counter to international human rights norms that all human beings, including transsexual persons, have dignity and rights as human beings and are entitled to enjoy them, and does not conform to the attitudes of countries around the world or the demands of the times.\\n나. Standard for Determining Whether Permission for Correction of the Gender Entry Should Be Granted\\n1) When determining whether to grant permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with minor children, the constitutional fundamental rights of the transsexual person himself or herself, such as human dignity and value, the right to pursue happiness, and the right to equality, must be guaranteed to the fullest extent, while at the same time the welfare of the child, including the child’s right to receive protection and care, must be kept in mind. Therefore, in such cases, in addition to whether the general requirements for permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person have been satisfied, the court must examine, by considering all circumstances such as the age and physical and mental condition of the minor children, the degree of the minor children’s consent to or understanding of the father’s or mother’s correction of the gender entry, the form of protection and upbringing of the minor children, the manner in which the transsexual person performs his or her role as father or mother, the relationship and bond the transsexual person has formed and maintained with the minor children and other family members, and other family circumstances, whether granting permission for correction of the gender entry of the transsexual person affects the welfare of the minor children, and determine whether to grant such permission.\\n2) In individual and concrete cases, the court must, according to such standards, closely examine the actual emotional, economic, and social circumstances experienced by the transitioned father or mother and the minor children, and make a substantive determination as to which decision protects the transsexual person’s fundamental human rights while also conforming to the welfare of the minor children, whether the disadvantages suffered by the minor children from granting permission for correction of the gender entry are markedly greater and more serious than restricting or infringing the transsexual person’s rights based on human dignity under the Constitution, and whether, despite the existence of alternatives that could reduce the disadvantages to the minor children, refusing permission for correction of the gender entry of the father or mother until the minor children reach adulthood and thereby forcing the transsexual person’s suffering arising from the mismatch between actual sex and the sex shown in the official record is consistent with the principle of proportionality. Without doing so, to treat the transsexual person’s correction of the gender entry as contrary to the welfare of the minor children based on vague and abstract concerns and uniformly and completely deny it may, in light of the balance among legal interests, not only infringe the transsexual person’s constitutional fundamental rights but also produce a result that undermines the substantive welfare of the minor children.\\n4. Change of Precedent\\nTherefore, the Supreme Court’s En Banc Decision dated September 2, 2011, 2009SEU117, which held to the effect that correction of the gender entry in the Family Relations Register of a transsexual person is not permitted when the transsexual person has minor children, as well as decisions to the same effect, are all to be changed to the extent they are contrary to the view of this decision.\\n5. Determination in This Case\\nWe examine the reasoning of the court below’s decision in light of the legal principles seen above. The court below cited the Supreme Court’s En Banc Decision dated September 2, 2011, 2009SEU117, and, viewing the existence of minor children as an independent negative requirement for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person, refused the permission application in this case merely on the ground that the Applicant has minor children, without specifically examining the various circumstances appearing in the record of this case and making a substantive determination. In the court below’s determination, there is a misapprehension of the legal principles concerning the constitutional fundamental rights under the Constitution’s Preamble to Article 10 that all citizens have dignity and value as human beings and the right to pursue happiness, Article 11(1) that all citizens are equal before the law, and the criteria for granting permission for correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person, and there is also an error affecting the judgment by failing to conduct the necessary trial. The Applicant’s assertion of the grounds for re-appeal pointing out this error is well-founded.\\n6. Conclusion\\nTherefore, we reverse the court below’s decision and remand the case to the court below for further trial and determination, and so decide as stated in the order. Except for the dissenting opinion of Justice Lee Dong-won, the opinions of the participating Justices were unanimous, and there are supplementary opinions to the majority opinion by Justice Park Jung-hwa, Justice Noh Jeong-hee, and Justice Lee Heung-gu, as well as supplementary opinions by Justice Kim Seon-su and Justice Oh Kyung-mi.\\n7. Dissenting Opinion of Justice Lee Dong-won\\nJustice Lee Dong-won’s dissenting opinion is as follows.\\n가. The previously existing Supreme Court’s En Banc Decision dated September 2, 2011, 2009SEU117(이하 ‘the Second En Banc Decision’이라 한다)은, if a transsexual person has minor children, correction of the gender entry is not permitted, held. As grounds, it stated that under our Civil Act system, in legally evaluating the sex of a person exercising parental authority, the welfare of the minor children must be considered first, and that if such permission were allowed, the special status relationship between the person exercising parental authority and the minor children and the negative impact on the welfare of the minor children would be significant.\\nThe majority opinion appears to view the Supreme Court’s Second En Banc Decision as newly establishing the fact that a transsexual person has minor children as an independent negative requirement for permission to correct the gender entry. However, even before the Second En Banc Decision, the Supreme Court had already, in its En Banc Decision dated June 22, 2006, 2004SEU42(이하 ‘the First En Banc Decision’이라 한다), presented the basic principle that, in order to permit correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person, “it must not cause a significant change in the status relationship with others or have a negative impact on society, and therefore must be socially acceptable.” The Second En Banc Decision merely clarified that the case of a transsexual person with minor children falls within a case contrary to such basic principle; it did not newly establish an independent negative requirement for permission to correct the gender entry.\\nBecause the Second En Banc Decision is consistent with our legal system and the welfare of minor children, and is also a rational decision conforming to the general common sense of society, it should be maintained as is. I cannot agree with the majority opinion attempting to change it. Below, I will examine the reasons in detail.\\n나. Article 36(1) of the Constitution provides: “Marriage and family life shall be founded and maintained on the basis of individual dignity and the equality of the sexes, and the State shall guarantee this.” This shows that our Constitution presupposes that the marriage and family system, the most basic unit of our society and the foundation of common life in all spheres, is founded and maintained through the union of differentiated sexes on the premise of the distinction between the sexes. In addition, the Constitution contains various provisions dividing men and women and requiring special protection of women within a certain range, and especially in the field of the marriage and family system, it requires the State to strive to protect women, that is, maternity, which is directly related to pregnancy and childbirth of children(Article 36(2)).\\nAlthough the provisions concerning kinship in our Civil Act(Part 4, Kinship) were amended several times since enactment in 1958 up to recent years, the provisions regarding the parent-child relationship in blood define the requirements for establishment and the rights and obligations on the premise that such relationship is formed by the birth of a child by a mother who conceived through sexual relations between the father and mother or through artificial insemination, and the provisions regarding legal parent-child relationships are not substantially different from those concerning the parent-child relationship in blood, except that there is no blood relation between them.\\nConsidering the text of the Constitution and the Civil Act and the history and structure of enactment and amendment thereof, it is clear that our legal system, including the Constitution and Civil Act, presupposes that a father is a male and a mother is a female. Therefore, under our Constitution, Civil Act, and other statutes, a female father or male mother cannot be permitted. Accordingly, granting permission for correction of the gender entry to a transsexual person who has children would amount to creating a parent-child relationship not permitted under our legal system. It goes without saying that such a new status relationship cannot be created without a legal basis. By contrast, because our statutes, including the Constitution and Civil Act, do not distinguish between male and female with respect to the sex of children, even if correction of the gender entry is permitted for a transsexual child, the parent-child relationship does not deviate from our legal system. The argument that, because correction of the gender entry of a transsexual child is possible, correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person who has children must also be possible is based on a failure to properly see the essence of the issue. This issue is also on a different level from the fact that correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person does not affect the existing status relationship and rights and obligations.\\nHowever, according to the Second En Banc Decision, if a transsexual person has minor children, correction of the gender entry is not permitted, whereas if a transsexual person has adult children, the conclusion is that correction of the gender entry may be permitted if, by comprehensively considering various circumstances, it is recognized that the person has the transitioned sex physically in social common sense; and it is true that this aspect is not consistent with the above legal system. Although it is not legally consistent to distinguish between cases where there are adult children and cases where there are minor children and to treat the permissibility of correction of the gender entry differently, this can be understood in that it was done by weighing the systematic conformity of our legal system and legal stability against the need for correction of the gender entry, considering that if the same legal logic were adhered to and correction of the gender entry were not permitted even when the transsexual person has adult children, the rights of the transsexual person would be excessively restricted. To claim, conversely, that because correction of the gender entry may be permitted when there are adult children, it must also be permitted when there are minor children, is to fail to properly appreciate the Supreme Court precedent that, while wrestling with legal logic and the necessity of correction of the gender entry, derived a harmonious solution.\\n다. In the First En Banc Decision, the Supreme Court took the position that correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person cannot be permitted in cases “where it causes a significant change in the status relationship with others or has a negative impact on society,” and in the Second En Banc Decision, “where a transsexual person has minor children” was given as a representative example. This stems from the fact that, from the transsexual person’s perspective, if correction of the gender entry is permitted, the person gains the benefit of full protection of constitutional fundamental rights, whereas from the perspective of the minor children in a parent-child relationship with the transsexual person, the status relationship or welfare is bound to be seriously adversely affected, and there is no legal basis sufficient to justify the disadvantages the children would suffer in such a case.\\nWhere a person with issues of sexual identity marries of his or her own choice and has children, or, even without marrying, has children, this is because the person has consented to accept the sex at birth and has decided to form family relations and carried that out; therefore, if the person changes sex at that stage, this cannot be viewed merely as a matter at the personal level. This is because a significant impact is caused to the status relationship or rights of others who formed family relations with that person. The issue of transsexuality at such a stage should be viewed as a matter of change of sex, not correction of the gender entry.\\nIt was possible in the existing First and Second En Banc Decisions to resolve the issue of a transsexual person changing sex through the legal theory of correction of the gender entry because the Court carefully examined whether the case fell within the category of “causing a significant change in the status relationship with others or having a negative impact on society,” and thereby preemptively blocked disadvantages that others would suffer. However, if the Supreme Court now adopts a completely different position and makes a decision requiring others to bear such disadvantages, this would go beyond the limitations of the legal theory of correction of the gender entry as originally contemplated by the First and Second En Banc Decisions.\\nFurthermore, such a decision by the Supreme Court will bring about significant changes to the family system, which has long been established as a core element of our society. In particular, this concerns essential issues in our society deeply related to ethical, philosophical, and religious issues, and should be approached at the level of change of sex with legal grounds prepared through legislative decision by the National Assembly, the representative organ of the people, after gathering the opinions of the general public and going through careful discussion and deliberation; it is not desirable to force an expansion of the legal theory of correction of the gender entry.\\nThe court must clearly recognize its responsibility for the performance and maintenance of family life guaranteed by the Constitution and for the maintenance and development of families, and must protect their dignity and value; it must also aim to improve the happiness and welfare of family members by assisting citizens to faithfully fulfill the legal, moral, and ethical duties they bear as members of families, and interpret and apply the law in a direction that avoids family dissolution(Framework Act on Healthy Families Articles 1, 4, and 9).\\n라. Our Civil Act provides that parents become the persons exercising parental authority over their minor children(Article 909(1)), that a person exercising parental authority has the right and duty to protect and educate the child(Article 913), and that in exercising parental authority, the welfare of the child must be considered first(Article 912). Although parental authority is provided in the form of a right in the statutory text, by its nature it has both the character of a right and the character of a duty, and in particular in modern times its aspect as a duty is more emphasized. Therefore, a person exercising parental authority must exercise it in a manner consistent with the “welfare of the child,” and in some cases must also endure restrictions on the fundamental rights of the individual person exercising parental authority for the “welfare of the child.”\\nSuch an interpretation is also consistent with the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child, which declares the principle of the “best interests of the child” that the interests of the child shall be a primary consideration in all actions concerning children(adopted on November 20, 1989, and ratified by our country, coming into force domestically on December 20, 1991).\\nFurthermore, in light of our society’s view of family, which particularly values bonds and consideration among family members, expecting a person exercising parental authority to refrain as much as possible from entering into the series of processes for transsexual transition and correction of the gender entry for the welfare of the child, and even if not possible, to maintain a more cautious and sincere attitude in deciding each step, is the minimum request for consideration that current our society can make of a person who, of his or her own choice, married the opposite sex, gave birth to children, and formed a family.\\nHowever, the majority opinion appears to prioritize the individual fundamental rights of the person exercising parental authority on the ground that it is difficult to conclude that the mere correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person in the Family Relations Register will harm the welfare of the minor children. If the concept of the “welfare of the child” is treated lightly on the ground that it is vague and abstract, and if claims regarding the possibility of its infringement are dismissed as empty, then not only the “welfare of the child” but ultimately also various precious values, invisible though they may be, that our society must protect are ignored.\\nMoreover, compared with the minor children of families whose parents have not undergone transsexual transition and correction of the gender entry, the mental confusion and shock suffered by minor children who have parents who have done so can be easily imagined, and irrespective of the social pros and cons regarding transsexuality or correction of the gender entry, social discrimination and prejudice against these matters are an undeniable reality. Since minor children who are not yet mature will be directly exposed to this reality and the suffering they may endure is sufficiently foreseeable, converting the circumstance that the welfare of the child is harmed into a mere issue of abstract possibility can only be seen as deliberately turning away from such a problem.\\nThe court, even when hearing and deciding on whether to permit correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person, should stand in a protective position and interpret and apply the law so as to prioritize the welfare of the child and avoid negative effects thereon, which is consistent with the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the provisions and purpose of the Civil Act.\\n마. Even if, as the majority opinion states, one were to take the position that the Court must determine whether permission for correction of the gender entry of the Applicant would specifically and seriously affect the minor children and significantly contradict their welfare before deciding whether to grant permission, in this case, considering the following circumstances in combination, the Applicant’s correction of the gender entry cannot be permitted, and therefore the court below’s decision must be maintained as is.\\n1) The Applicant formed a parent-child relationship with the children by giving birth to them through sexual relations with the opposite sex by the Applicant’s own choice. In such a situation, it does not seem excessive to require the Applicant to place the welfare of the minor children first.\\n2) In this case, the Applicant has concealed from the children the fact that the Applicant is their father and is pretending to be an aunt. Such a situation cannot be regarded as a case where a natural family relationship has formed according to the transitioned sex of the parent. Nevertheless, if the Applicant’s correction of the gender entry is hastily permitted, there is ample room to regard that as contrary to the welfare of the child.\\n3) There may be an argument that, since the Applicant is concealing his or her status from the children by pretending to be an aunt, and correction of the gender entry would merely change the sex of the Applicant who had been pretending to be an aunt, there would be no additional mental confusion or shock for the minor children. Such an argument is possible only when the issue of a transsexual person’s correction of the gender entry is viewed solely as an issue after the point at which the sex is corrected and entered in the Family Relations Register. The court must not merely measure fragmentary advantages or disadvantages after a certain point, but must seriously and cautiously consider what decision is best for the welfare of the child by comprehensively examining all circumstances anticipated throughout the process before and after.\\n4) In ordinary cases, the mental shock or confusion of minor children is more likely to arise not during the correction of the gender entry in the Family Relations Register concerning a transsexual person, but from the actual change in the physical appearance of the father or mother that occurs beforehand. However, in this case, the minor children knew the Applicant as an aunt rather than as a father, and thus did not experience the Applicant’s physical appearance change. Rather, they are very likely to experience mental shock or confusion later in the process of inspecting or obtaining the family relation certificate and thereby becoming aware of it.\\nThere may be an argument that if minor children suffer mental shock, it can be addressed through psychological counseling or treatment. However, that is not a position that a court, which must interpret and apply the law by prioritizing the welfare of minor children whose ability to adapt has not matured and whose sensitivity is acute, should adopt.\\n바. In light of the above legal principles and factual circumstances, the court below’s action in upholding the first-instance decision dismissing the Applicant’s application for correction of the gender entry, where the Applicant has minor children, is proper, and there is no error such as that alleged as grounds for the re-appeal. Therefore, the re-appeal should be dismissed.\\nFor the foregoing reasons, I state that I cannot agree with the majority opinion.\\n8. Supplementary Opinion to the Majority Opinion by Justice Park Jung-hwa, Justice Noh Jeong-hee, and Justice Lee Heung-gu\\nWhile supplementing the majority opinion, I wish to rebut, to the extent necessary, some of the arguments presented in the dissenting opinion.\\nThe dissenting opinion says that the Second En Banc Decision should be maintained because it is a rational decision consistent with our legal system, the welfare of minor children, and the general common sense of society. However, such dissenting opinion is difficult to accept because it is contrary to the purpose of the First En Banc Decision, infringes the essential content of the transsexual person’s fundamental rights, and may also run counter to the welfare of minor children. The reasons are as follows.\\n가. Gender identity refers to the internal and personal experience and deep sense of belonging that a human being feels with respect to gender, irrespective of the sex assigned at birth. Every human being, through gender identity in society, recognizes the self and completes a personal narrative by reinterpreting and reconstructing personal experiences and giving them meaning. The right concerning gender identity is one of the principal contents of the general personality right derived from the Preamble to Article 10 of the Constitution, which prescribes human dignity, value, and the right to pursue happiness, and has significant meaning in the very existence of the individual or the mode of life.\\nA transsexual person refers to a person whose manifestation of gender identity differs from the biological sex possessed at birth. Human society has divided human beings into male or female based on biological sex at birth and regarded this as an unchangeable absolute, and by recognizing transsexual persons as a third existence that is neither male nor female, or by denying the very existence of those who do clearly exist in actual society, has religiously and socially forced transsexual persons to abandon or conceal their own gender identity. However, it has long been medically, scientifically, and philosophically verified that transsexual persons are also one form of human existence. Nevertheless, it cannot be denied that such a custom, which is essentially no different from denying the very existence of human beings, still persists with respect to minorities in our society. The State has a duty to uphold the rights concerning gender identity of transsexual persons guaranteed by the Preamble to Article 10 of the Constitution, which prescribes human dignity, value, and the right to pursue happiness, even in order to overcome this reality.\\n나. All citizens have the right to have the sex corresponding to their gender identity indicated consistently in the official record. This right has particular significance for transsexual persons. Because a transsexual person who has acquired a gender identity different from the biological sex at birth is publicly recorded in the Family Relations Register according to biological classification, such a person inevitably faces serious problems arising from inconsistency between reality and public record during the process of transition. If the State does not guarantee a procedural right to correct the official record so that it accords with their true gender identity, this infringes the essential content of the transsexual person’s right concerning gender identity, which is a fundamental right under the Preamble to Article 10 of the Constitution.\\n다. When fundamental rights or public interests and other legal interests conflict, the issue must be resolved according to the principle of practical concordance of legal interests(norm-harmonizing interpretation). Because restricting the right of a transsexual person to correction of the gender entry in the Family Relations Register constitutes an infringement of the essential content of the transsexual person’s human dignity and value and the right to pursue happiness, and the degree of restriction of fundamental rights is very large and serious, there must be serious and clear circumstances showing the necessity to protect or realize other legal interests or values through such restriction, and that there is no alternative other than such restriction. In other words, the right of a transsexual person to correction of the gender entry can secure the justification of its restriction only if it is harmoniously adjusted in a direction that recognizes the dignity of the transsexual person to the fullest extent even in relation to minor children.\\nHowever, according to the Second En Banc Decision, a court dealing with a case of correction of the gender entry by a transsexual person with minor children must refuse permission for correction of the gender entry merely because the person has minor children, without conducting a concrete hearing as to what constitutes the welfare of the minor children, what kind of infringement of welfare may occur depending on the parent’s correction of the gender entry, or whether that infringement is serious and clear. Even in cases where the relevant minor children accept the transsexual father or mother as having the transitioned sex and live stably according to that status while hoping that the father’s or mother’s gender entry in the Family Relations Register will be corrected to reflect reality, the court has no choice but to deny it. This conclusion creates a contradictory situation in which the court, which must protect the rights of transsexual persons and minor children and ensure their peaceful lives, infringes both their rights and destabilizes them. This is the result of understanding the value of the welfare of the minor children in an abstract and conceptual manner and disregarding the substantive meaning of correction of the gender entry for a transsexual person with minor children in a concrete case.\\n라. The dissenting opinion says that the First En Banc Decision presented as a basic principle that, in order to permit correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person, it must not cause a significant change in the status relationship with others or have a negative impact on society, and that the Second En Banc Decision did not newly establish the fact that a transsexual person has minor children as an independent negative requirement for permission to correct the gender entry, but merely clarified the purport of the First En Banc Decision. However, this interpretation by the dissenting opinion unjustly narrows the significance of the First En Banc Decision in order to maintain the Second En Banc Decision denying correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with minor children.\\nThe First En Banc Decision declared as a principle that, in determining sex, biological factors and mental and social factors must be comprehensively considered, and accordingly, if a person can be recognized as having the transitioned sex, then a transsexual person must be permitted correction of the gender entry in the official record because, unlike at birth, the transitioned sex is to be legally evaluated as that person’s sex. Also, contrary to the dissenting opinion’s assertion, the First En Banc Decision announced that “the effect of a decision granting permission for correction of the gender entry or the correction of the sex entry based thereon does not affect the existing status relationship and rights and obligations.” In the supplementary opinion to the majority opinion, it was also made clear that “it should be understood not as establishing a negative requirement that the transsexual person must not cause a change in the status relationship with others or a negative impact on society, but rather that if the transsexual person is confirmed to be a transsexual person in the true sense, and furthermore if correction of the gender entry is made accordingly, the effect may be permitted as long as it does not retroactively have a significant effect on existing status relationships, etc., and the effect is limited to a restricted scope.”\\n마. The dissenting opinion says that because the Constitution and our legal system, including the Civil Act, clearly presuppose that a father is male and a mother is female, granting permission for correction of the gender entry to a transsexual person who has children would create a parent-child relationship not permitted under our legal system and thus cannot be allowed.\\nHowever, it cannot be said that a transsexual parent’s correction of the gender entry creates a parent-child relationship or new status relationship not permitted under our legal system. The fact that a parent is a transsexual person does not mean that the person is no longer the child’s biological parent or that the child is not the transsexual person’s biological child. A transsexual person and his or her child retain their unique rights and duties as parent and child regardless of whether it is before or after the transition. The fact that there is no appropriate term other than father or mother to refer to a transitioned parent does not mean that the original rights and duties or status relationship they had as parent and child disappear, cease, or become void. This was already declared in the First En Banc Decision.\\n바. Article 36(1) of the Constitution provides: “Marriage and family life shall be founded and maintained on the basis of individual dignity and the equality of the sexes, and the State shall guarantee this.” The dissenting opinion, using the expression “equality of the sexes” in the above provision, says that our Constitution presupposes that marriage and the family system are founded and maintained on the basis of the distinction between the sexes and the union between differentiated sexes, and that the correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person who has children is not permitted by our Constitution and laws, but that the Second En Banc Decision, although not legally consistent, distinguished between cases where the transsexual person has adult children and cases where the person has minor children by weighing the systematic conformity of our legal system and legal stability against the need for correction of the gender entry, and accordingly treated the permissibility of correction of the gender entry differently.\\nFirst, it must be pointed out that the dissenting opinion unjustly interprets the meaning of the Second En Banc Decision regarding correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with children. In the Second En Banc Decision, the Supreme Court did not expressly state the view that, in the case of a transsexual person with minor children, because our Constitution presupposes the distinction between the sexes in the marriage and family system, correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with children is not permitted under our Constitution and laws, or that correction of the gender entry of a transsexual person with children causes a change in the children’s status relationship or rights and obligations. Rather, the Second En Banc Decision reaffirmed and declared the legal principle of the First En Banc Decision, which held that the permission for correction of the gender entry in the Family Relations Register for a transsexual person is a decision intended to confirm the current true sex newly legally evaluated according to transsexuality, and therefore the effect of a decision granting correction or the correction of the sex entry in the Family Relations Register based thereon does not affect the existing status relationship and rights and obligations. It only held that, in the case of minor children, in light of the significant negative impact of a parent’s correction of the gender entry on the welfare of the minor children due to social discrimination and prejudice, the parental duty to protect the minor children from such negative impact, and other circumstances, “considering that it is difficult to conclude that merely because the effect of correction of the sex entry does not affect ‘existing’ parent-child relationships and other legal relationships, all of the newly arising difficulties in the living relationship of the minor children are thereby resolved,” correction of the gender entry is not permitted when the transsexual person has minor children.\\nIf Article 36(1) of the Constitution is interpreted as the dissenting opinion does, it leads to results not harmonious with the provisions of Article 10, Article 11(1), and Article 37(1) of the Constitution. With respect to the protection of the family community, together with Article 36(1), one must apply the Preamble to Article 10 of the Constitution, which guarantees human dignity and value and the right to pursue happiness, the latter sentence of Article 10 of the Constitution, which states that “the State shall have the duty to confirm and guarantee the inviolable fundamental human rights of individuals,” Article 11(1), which guarantees the right to equality, and Article 37(1), which states that “the freedoms and rights of citizens shall not be disregarded on the ground that they are not enumerated in the Constitution.” Ultimately, the State must equally protect the family community of a transsexual person and his or her children without discrimination, just like any other family community. Furthermore, because Article 36(1) of the Constitution declares that, together with the meaning and preciousness of the family community, they must be based on the ideology of “gender equality” and individual dignity, and that the State protects and guarantees them, it cannot be used as a basis for excluding them from protection according to the type of family life. Article 36(1) of the Constitution should be interpreted prospectively as including the family community of a transsexual person with minor children as a protected subject.\\nThe importance of the family community cannot be overemphasized, and this is no different in the case of transsexual persons. The bond between a transsexual person and his or her family members must also be socially respected and legally protected without discrimination. If transsexual persons and their family members cherish the family community they have formed and wish to continue living while maintaining that bond, the State and society have the duty to respect such wishes to the fullest extent and guarantee their family life. In the case of modern family communities, including the family community of transsexual persons, which are appearing in diverse forms, actively accepting and protecting them within the existing family order to the extent that they do not violate social order and the public welfare strengthens the diversity and soundness of our society and reinforces the safety net surrounding society, thereby promoting the ultimate welfare of members of society.\\n사. In our society, transsexual persons still must endure, in daily life and legally, the environment of discrimination and exclusion, the division of the self, and the threat to existence, and suffer the pain of not being able to fully complete their narrative in accordance with their actual gender identity. Because of their appearance or mannerisms, transsexual persons are easily exposed to various forms of danger, including sexual violence, and this increases even more when the sex they personally disclose does not match the legal sex indicated in official certificates or documents such as identity cards and passports.\\nHowever noble the light of the constitutional spirit that guarantees human dignity and value may be, if that light does not shine equally on members of society, including transsexual minorities, its meaning will fade. Institutional foundations must be laid so that transsexual persons may seek their life according to their true gender identity, and efforts must be made to improve the culture of discrimination that persists in reality. Through this, the constitutional guarantees of human dignity and value and the realization of fundamental rights can become substantive, not merely slogans.\\nThe First En Banc Decision was the fruit of such efforts. The Supreme Court, empathizing with the hardships transsexual persons must endure as a minority, declared that they, as equal members of our society, have the right to request correction of the gender entry in accordance with their gender identity as an extension of human dignity and value and the right to pursue happiness. Correction of the gender entry for transsexual persons does not solve all problems, but it is an important starting point for solving them. Starting from this, in order to truly solve their difficulties and remedy violations of fundamental rights, the voices of transsexual persons and their families must be institutionally reflected through legislation. Since the First En Banc Decision, for 16 years, the establishment of a legal system for transsexual persons has been delayed, and transsexual persons who must still remain in the shadow of exclusion are urgently calling for the guarantee of equal rights. There is a need to listen to the voices of transsexual persons, which resound breaking the icy silence created by the established rigid order, and to adopt an attitude of empathy for their suffering. While emphasizing once again the importance of the judiciary’s role in protecting the rights of transsexual persons, a minority in our society, and the urgency of legislative measures concerning correction of the gender entry, I state this supplementary opinion to the majority opinion.\"}"}

\"원고들이 소외 2의 친생자가 아님을 확인하고, 소외 2는 원고들에게 3,500,000원을 지급하되, 원고들은 더 이상의 금원청구를 하지 아니한다.\"는 내용의 재판상 화해가 성립되었다. And as the 인지무효 확인심판 became final and conclusive, 원고들은 소외 2의 호적에서 제적되고 일가창립에 의하여 각각 호주로 되어 부(부)란은 공란으로, 모(모)는 소외 1로 한 호적이 각 편제되었다.\\n(5) After the above 재판상 화해가 성립된 다음, 소외 1은 another man과 혼인하고 원고들에게서 손을 떼었고, meanwhile 소외 2는 원고들에게 학비를 주어 유학을 보내기도 하고 그들의 결혼식에도 참석하기도 하는 등 실질적으로 원고들의 아버지 역할을 수행하여 오다가 1994. 11. 30. 사망하였고, 원고들은 1995. 1. 4. 이 사건 인지청구의 소를 제기하였다.\\n2. Regarding the grounds of appeal on the 본안전 항변 부분\\nThe 원심은, 이 사건 인지청구가 already 확정된 인지무효 확인심판 및 원고들과 소외 2 사이에 친생자관계가 없음을 확인하는 내용이 포함되어 있는 조정과 재판상 화해의 기판력들에 저촉되고, 그 조정과 재판상 화해의 내용에 비추어 금반언의 원칙에 반하며, 또한 사실상 인지청구권의 포기 내지 실효 이후에 소멸된 소권을 행사하는 것으로서 소권의 남용에 해당한다는 참가인들의 주장에 대하여, 인지무효확인의 확정심판은 소외 2 스스로 원고들을 그의 친생자로 인정하여 출생신고를 한 바 없는데도 소외 1에 의해 그러한 행위를 한 것처럼 호적상 기재가 되어 있으니 그 출생신고에 의한 임의 인지가 무효임을 확인한다는 것이 심판대상임이 명백하고, therefore its 기판력 역시 소외 2의 출생신고에 의한 임의 인지가 무효라는 점에 한하여 발생할 뿐이며, 나아가 소외 2와 원고들 사이에 친생자관계가 존재하는지의 여부에 대해서까지 그 확정심판의 효력이 미치는 것은 아니므로, 그 확정심판의 효력은 원고들이 소외 2와의 사이에 친생자관계가 존재함을 전제로 하여 재판상 인지를 구하는 이 사건 청구에는 미치지 아니하고, 친생자관계의 존부확인과 같이 현행 가사소송법상의 가류 가사소송사건에 해당하는 청구는 성질상 당사자가 임의로 처분할 수 없는 사항을 대상으로 하는 것으로서 이에 관하여 조정이나 재판상 화해가 성립되더라도 효력이 있을 수 없으므로 (대법원 1968. 4. 6. 선고 65다139, 140 판결 참조), 위의 조정이나 재판상 화해는 원고들과 소외 2 사이에 친생자관계가 없음을 확인한다는 점에 관한 한 그 효력이 없어 기판력이 생길 여지가 없고, 또 인지청구권은 포기할 수 없고, 포기하였다 하더라도 효력이 발생할 수 없는 것이므로 (대법원 1987. 1. 20. 선고 85므70 판결 참조), 조정이나 재판상 화해로 인하여 원고들이 인지청구권을 포기하였다거나 실권하였다고 할 수 없으며, 따라서 이 사건 청구가 금반언의 원칙에 반한다거나 권리남용에 해당한다고도 할 수 없다고 판단하여, 참가인들의 주장을 모두 배척하였다.\\n기록에 비추어 살펴보면, 원심의 위와 같은 판단은 옳고, 거기에 기판력이나 쟁점효, 권리실효, 권리포기 또는 금반언의 원칙 등에 관한 법리를 오해한 위법이 있다고 할 수 없다. 이 점에 관한 상고이유는 받아들일 수 없다.\\n3. Regarding the grounds of appeal on the merits\\n원심판결 이유에 의하면, 원심은 그 채택 증거인 유전자감정촉탁결과와 사실조회결과에 의하여 망 소외 2가 원고들의 친부일 가능성을 배제할 수 없고, 부권확률이 원고 2의 경우 낮게는 88.029%, 높게는 99.9999999998%, 원고 2의 경우 낮게는 91.891%, 높게는 99.99999999995%인 점을 인정한 다음, 여기에 위에서 본 사실관계를 종합하여, 원고들은 소외 1과 망 소외 2 사이에서 출생한 망 소외 2의 친생자임을 인정하고, 원고들의 이 사건 인지청구를 모두 인용하였다.\\n관련 증거들을 기록에 대조하여 살펴보면, 이러한 원심의 사실인정은 수긍이 가고, 거기에 채증법칙 위반이나 심리미진으로 인한 사실오인, 판단유탈 또는 입증책임에 관한 법리오해 등의 위법이 있다고 할 수 없다. 이 점에 관한 상고이유 또한 받아들이지 아니한다.\\n4. Therefore, all 상고를 기각하고, 상고비용은 패소자들의 부담으로 하기로 하여 관여 법관의 일치된 의견으로 주문과 같이 판결한다."}

question: Which of the following statements regarding 주관적 범죄성립요건 is correct? (Where there is a dispute, according to 판례)
A: With 살의를 가지고, if the actor 피해자를 구타하여 (ⓐ행위), and when the victim loses consciousness and goes limp, mistakenly believes the victim to be dead and buries the victim in sand for the purpose of 증거를 인멸하기 위해 (ⓑ행위), and it is found that the victim died from act (b), since the direct cause of death is act (b), 살인미수죄가 성립한다.
B: In order for an actor’s conduct to qualify as 긴급피난, it is sufficient that the actor has only 긴급피난상황에 대한 인식; an intent to avoid the 위난 is not also required.
C: Where a person, with the purpose of 모해, instigates a person who does not have the purpose of 모해 to commit 위증, under the principle of 공범종속성, the offense of 위증교사, rather than 모해위증교사, is established.
D: If a witness, being mistaken, testifies to content contrary to objective facts without awareness that it is contrary to his or her own memory, 위증의 범의 can be recognized.
E: Where an actor who accidentally received a mistaken remittance from a trading company that is in litigation over a claim for payment of the price of goods refuses to return the mistakenly remitted money with the intent to exercise a lawful right of 상계 against the price of the goods, the establishment of the 불법영득의사, which is an element of 횡령죄, may be denied.
